item.description: MadsLorentzen/ai-job-search is an AI-powered job application framework built on Claude Code that runs locally on your machine. It is an independent open-source project, not affiliated with Anthropic.

Cursor, the author says, was his first strong taste of what AI coding can do, while Codex feels less like a coding assistant and more like an autonomous super-agent, closer to the next stage of tooling. Useful for developers weighing which AI coding tool to adopt.

item.title: [infoq] DoorDash的Flux在云端智能体上运行130000个工程任务
item.description: DoorDash moved engineering agents off developer laptops onto Flux, its own cloud platform, which automated 130,000 engineering tasks in a single month of 2026 while supporting more than 25,000 automated code reviews and 10,000 triggers per week. Flux rests on four primitives: cloud Sandboxes, an MCP gateway, reusable Playbooks and invocation surfaces. Sandboxes run in Firecracker microVMs, with a p95 end-to-end setup target under five seconds.

item.description: Alibaba Cloud's CTO R&D line published interim results from its push toward an AI-native engineering organization. At the Yunqi conference forum, VP Tang Hong described agent computing as "model + harness + context" and argued the real dividing line is agents entering production pipelines, with organization-native operation as the long-term goal. This post covers the organizational view only; seven hands-on practices will follow as separate articles.

item.title: [infoq] 大批API账户被刷爆！OpenCode遭黑客围攻48小时，官方甩锅“蒸馏攻击”被质疑
item.description: OpenCode says an old system being retired was accessed without authorization, potentially exposing third-party model API keys for 1.4% of its cloud Console users; some victims saw single-day bills above $1,700, and Anthropic, OpenAI and Google moved to revoke affected keys. Co-founder Dax Raad said attacks continued for 48 hours, while the company's framing of the incident as a large-scale "model distillation attack" drew pushback from developers.

item.title: [infoq] 随着可观测性模式日趋成熟，OpenTelemetry 将 Kubernetes Attribute Processor 提升为稳定版本
item.description: OpenTelemetry has promoted its Kubernetes Attribute Processor to 1.0.0. It enriches logs, metrics and traces with Pod, namespace, node and workload metadata, turning generic telemetry into data you can query and correlate by Kubernetes context. The stable release follows Semantic Conventions v1.42.0 and is not fully backward compatible: container.image.tag becomes container.image.tags and k8s.pod.labels becomes k8s.pod.label, so dashboards, alerts and queries using the old names must be updated.

item.title: [hackernews] Linux 7.3
item.description: Linux 7.3 is out: Linus Torvalds released the kernel on October 18, with 18,765 non-merge commits from 3,021 developers, 807 of them first-time contributors, which the release note calls a record on all fronts. Changes include extensions to binfmt_misc. The 7.4 merge window opens the next day, though Torvalds' family vacation will make his schedule unusual. Kernel and distro maintainers should start evaluating it.

It targets state-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting, works zero-shot out of the box, and is built to run efficiently on CPU. Teams that need forecasting without training their own model, or without GPU capacity, are the obvious audience.

item.description: A Juejin post describes how the author built an AI Agent desktop workbench on top of Pi. Its main argument is not to reinvent the wheel: the model calls, message loop, tool protocol and permission system do not need to be written from scratch. It is aimed at developers who want their own agent desktop tool without rebuilding the plumbing first.

item.title: [zhihu] 微软最新研究称 Agent 的「长记忆」可能是毒药，造成这一现象的原因是什么？
item.description: A Zhihu discussion prompted by a Microsoft study suggesting that long-term memory in agents may be harmful rather than helpful, with the poster asking what causes the effect. The linked page isn't summarized here; details beyond the title aren't available.

item.title: [juejin] 用了一个月 WorkBuddy，聊聊我的真实感受
item.description: A heavy GPT user of more than two years, who had been calling the API through a third-party relay because of network issues, writes up his impressions after a month with WorkBuddy. The piece works through everyday tasks such as drafting proposals, editing copy and organizing materials, so it is aimed at people comparing AI tools for daily work.

item.title: [juejin] 甲方只给了一张卫星截图，我用 Three.js + Blender 建了一座 3D 能源站
item.description: Working from just one satellite screenshot, the author rebuilt a 3D integrated energy station with Three.js and Blender: reverse-engineering the design camera, scripting the model, baking a night scene in Cycles, animating a heavy truck backing into place, running an operations simulation, and checking fidelity pixel by pixel with overlays. Worth reading if you care about 3D reconstruction and graphics pipeline practice.

item.title: [juejin] 别再死磕纯技术了：2026 年程序员的 7 条真实出路
item.description: A career piece that lays out seven paths programmers are actually taking, with each one's real entry bar, trade-offs and the kind of person it suits. It's framed around AI tooling going mainstream, shrinking hiring at big companies and the 35-year age cutoff, so it speaks to developers weighing a change of track.
